Research Portfolio

Connecting academic rigor with applied impact

Author

Your Name

Welcome

This portfolio presents a body of work that connects academic research, applied analytics, and decision focused data work. My background includes university based research, peer reviewed scholarship, and leadership in real world projects that support organizations, agencies, and stakeholders who need credible evidence for action.

I build projects that combine methodological rigor with practical use. Across both academic and industry settings, my work has focused on asking clear questions, using appropriate data and methods, and producing results that help people make better decisions.

NoteWhat you will find here

This site is designed for hiring audiences, collaborators, and general readers who want to understand both my research background and my applied project experience.

Professional profile

I am a researcher and applied data leader with experience spanning peer reviewed scholarship, program evaluation, data infrastructure, analytics, and public facing decision support. My academic work developed a strong foundation in research design, causal reasoning, and communication. My current work extends those same strengths into real world settings where data must be translated into operational, policy, and strategic value.

My approach is grounded in a simple principle: strong research should be useful. That means building analyses that are technically sound, transparent in their assumptions, and closely tied to the questions that matter most to decision makers.

How to read this portfolio

This site is organized around problems and methods rather than around a strict separation between academic and industry work. That structure is intentional. The same core skills, research design, data integration, analytic reasoning, and communication, support both peer reviewed scholarship and applied impact.

You can explore the site in three ways:

For hiring committees and employers

Focus on the sections on applied projects, case studies, methods in practice, and selected accomplishments. These sections highlight the kinds of questions I work on, the systems I build, and the ways analysis has informed decisions and action.

For academic and research collaborators

Focus on publications, research themes, and methodological contributions. These sections highlight the scholarly foundation of my work and the research traditions that continue to shape my applied practice.

For general readers

Focus on the plain language summaries and case studies. These sections explain the substance of the work without requiring specialized technical knowledge.

Selected strengths

Rigorous research design

My training and publication record reflect long experience with research design, quantitative and qualitative reasoning, longitudinal analysis, and evidence synthesis.

Applied analytics

I design analyses, reporting systems, dashboards, and data products that help organizations move from raw information to action.

Data infrastructure and reproducibility

Communication across audiences

Research and practice themes

Causal inference and program evaluation

A substantial share of my academic and applied work asks whether a program, intervention, or institutional process made a measurable difference. In academic settings, this often took the form of peer reviewed research using longitudinal or comparative designs. In applied settings, it involves helping organizations evaluate initiatives, interpret outcome patterns, and understand where evidence is strong and where uncertainty remains.

Example academic contributions

  • Publication or paper title one, with a one sentence summary of the question and contribution.
  • Publication or paper title two, with a one sentence summary of the question and contribution.

Example applied work

  • Project evaluating outcomes across programs, agencies, or organizational units.
  • Decision support work that helped stakeholders compare results over time or across groups.

Education, labor markets, and social outcomes

Much of my work has focused on how people move through institutions and into longer term outcomes. That includes questions about education, training, workforce participation, and broader social impact. In academic work, these questions often appear as formal research contributions. In applied work, they often take the form of dashboards, reports, or analytic frameworks that support planning and accountability.

Example academic contributions

  • Publication or paper title, with plain language explanation.
  • Publication or paper title, with plain language explanation.

Example applied work

  • Linked administrative data project tracking student, workforce, or program outcomes.
  • Reporting framework that translated complex outcome data into decision relevant indicators.

Data systems, infrastructure, and evidence use

Real world impact depends not only on analysis, but also on trustworthy systems. Part of my work centers on designing data pipelines, reproducible reporting, analytic environments, and governance conscious processes that allow organizations to use data responsibly and consistently.

Example academic contributions

  • Work related to methods, data integration, or reproducible research.

Example applied work

  • Building or improving data pipelines, documentation systems, or automated reporting.
  • Creating shared analytic frameworks that allow teams to generate repeatable evidence products.

Selected case studies

Case study 1, translating research into program evaluation

Context

This project focused on a practical question with real implications for decision making. Stakeholders needed to know whether observed patterns reflected meaningful differences in outcomes, and whether those patterns suggested opportunities for intervention or improvement.

Approach

I worked across the stages of the analytic process, from clarifying the question and assessing the available data to designing the analysis and communicating the results. The work required balancing methodological rigor with the limits of real world data, including missingness, administrative constraints, and reporting timelines.

Impact

The result was not just an analysis, but a decision support resource. The project helped stakeholders move from descriptive reporting toward evidence informed interpretation and action.

Case study 2, building infrastructure for reproducible analytics

Context

In many settings, the central challenge is not a single analysis but the lack of a sustainable process for producing reliable information. This kind of work often requires connecting multiple data sources, documenting transformations, and creating workflows that others can maintain.

Approach

I designed or contributed to a reproducible workflow that supported recurring analysis and reporting. This included data preparation, documentation, quality checks, and outputs tailored to stakeholder needs.

Impact

This work improved consistency, reduced manual effort, and increased confidence in the resulting evidence products. It also made future analysis easier and more transparent.

Portfolio note

Add links here to technical documentation, data pipeline summaries, or example outputs.

case study 3, communicating complex evidence to non technical audiences

context

High quality analysis has limited value if decision makers cannot interpret it. Many of my projects have required translating complex methods and results into forms that are accessible without sacrificing accuracy.

approach

I developed plain language summaries, visualizations, presentations, dashboards, and structured narratives that helped audiences understand what the data showed, what it did not show, and what action might follow.

impact

The resulting products supported broader engagement with evidence and helped bridge the gap between technical analysis and practical decision making.

methods in practice

The methods I use have remained remarkably consistent across academic and industry settings, even when the form of the deliverable changes.

research design

I begin by clarifying the decision context, the unit of analysis, the outcome of interest, and the assumptions required to draw conclusions. This is as important in applied analytics as it is in formal research.

longitudinal and linked data analysis

Many of my projects involve connecting records across systems or following people, programs, or organizations over time. These designs support stronger inference and more meaningful measurement than one time snapshots alone.

reproducible workflows

I prioritize documented, repeatable analytic processes. In practice, this often means version controlled code, structured data pipelines, literate programming, and outputs that can be updated as new data arrive.

communication and decision support

I treat communication as part of the analytic workflow, not as an afterthought. A methodologically sophisticated result has the greatest value when it is also understandable and actionable.
